Le 11 décembre 2024, Julien Matter, nouveau Chef de Mission de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) en Guinée, a rencontré les journalistes locaux lors d’un café-presse pour discuter des activités actuelles de MSF en Guinée, des défis humanitaires en cours et des projets menés par l’organisation dans le pays.
Cette rencontre a permis aux journalistes de poser des questions sur les enjeux majeurs auxquels MSF est confrontée sur le terrain. Julien Matter a répondu aux questions des journalistes concernant les défis liés à l’accès humanitaire dans certaines zones rurales du pays, ainsi que la gestion des épidémies récurrentes, telles que la rougeole.
Origines et principes de MSF
Julien Matter a rappelé les origines de MSF, créée il y a 50 ans par des journalistes et des médecins. L’organisation repose sur un principe fondamental : le témoignage. « Le médecin soigne, mais le journaliste peut faire en sorte que la situation change », a-t-il expliqué. Il a également évoqué les défis constants rencontrés par MSF, comme les entraves à l’aide humanitaire, citant notamment la situation actuelle à Gaza et dans d’autres parties du monde.
Rôle historique de MSF en Guinée
Le Chef de Mission de MSF a indiqué que son organisation a joué un rôle crucial dans l’assistance humanitaire aux réfugiés fuyant les guerres civiles au Libéria et en Sierra Leone, entre 1990-2000, en construisant et gérant des camps à Nzérékoré, Guéckédou, Forécariah, et Macenta. L’organisation a également mis en place des solutions durables pour l’eau potable et l’assainissement dans ces camps.
Combat contre le VIH/SIDA à Conakry
À Donka, MSF a créé un centre d’excellence pour le traitement du VIH avancé. En 2023, 917 patients y ont été hospitalisés, avec une nette réduction du taux de mortalité. M. Matter a également évoqué l’introduction de nouvelles techniques diagnostiques et la formation continue des médecins et infirmiers locaux. Il a souligné les efforts de recherche opérationnelle, notamment sur les résistances virales, et a insisté sur l’importance de la gratuité des soins et du dépistage. MSF continue de former des patients experts et de développer des stratégies ciblées pour atteindre les populations vulnérables.
Réponse aux urgences épidémiologiques
M. Matter a précisé que MSF collabore étroitement avec le ministère de la Santé et l’Agence Nationale de Sécurité Sanitaire (ANSS) pour renforcer les capacités locales de gestion des épidémies. Il a souligné l’importance de la formation continue des professionnels de santé et de l’intégration de la recherche opérationnelle, en particulier avec le déploiement de nouveaux services comme les soins palliatifs.
Projet Palu et renforcement des capacités à Kouroussa
Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le paludisme à Kouroussa, MSF a concentré ses efforts sur les soins, la formation du personnel soignant, l’appui logistique et matériel, ainsi que sur des stratégies adaptées pendant les pics de transmission. Julien Matter a décrit ce projet comme une illustration de l’engagement de MSF dans les interventions de santé publique à long terme.
La santé environnementale en Guinée
En Guinée, Médecins Sans Frontières accorde aussi une attention particulière à la santé environnementale. C’est pourquoi elle a construit et réhabilité des forages, mais s’est également impliquée dans la gestion moderne des déchets médicaux et les initiatives de sensibilisation aux bonnes pratiques d’hygiène.
Indépendance et financement de MSF
Avec plus de 50 ans d’expérience, MSF travaille aujourd’hui dans 70 pays, financée à 98 % par des fonds privés, garantissant ainsi son indépendance. Julien Matter a rappelé que les interventions de MSF, basées sur « l’impartialité, la neutralité et l’indépendance », mettent le patient au centre des préoccupations et bénéficient d’une logistique efficace permettant d’intervenir rapidement en cas de catastrophe ou d’épidémie.
À travers ses actions diversifiées en Guinée, Médecins Sans Frontières continue de démontrer son engagement à répondre aux besoins urgents en matière de santé tout en renforçant les capacités locales. L’organisation œuvre non seulement à fournir des soins immédiats et essentiels, mais aussi à long terme, en favorisant la formation des professionnels de santé et le développement d’infrastructures durables. En restant fidèle à ses principes d’indépendance, d’impartialité et de neutralité, MSF renforce son rôle clé dans la réponse humanitaire en Guinée, avec pour priorité le bien-être des populations vulnérables et la résilience des systèmes de santé locaux face aux défis de santé publique.
a1401.en:
MSF in Guinea: Humanitarian responses to health emergencies and strengthening local capacities

On 11 December 2024, Julien Matter, the new Head of Mission of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Guinea, met local journalists at a press café to discuss MSF's current activities in Guinea, the ongoing humanitarian challenges and the projects carried out by the organisation in the country.

This meeting allowed journalists to ask questions about the major issues MSF faces in the field. Julien Matter answered journalists' questions concerning the challenges linked to humanitarian access in certain rural areas of the country, as well as the management of recurrent epidemics, such as measles.

Origins and principles of MSF

Julien Matter recalled the origins of MSF, created 50 years ago by journalists and doctors. The organisation rests on a fundamental principle: testimony. "The doctor treats, but the journalist can make the situation change," he explained. He also evoked the constant challenges encountered by MSF, such as obstacles to humanitarian aid, citing notably the current situation in Gaza and in other parts of the world.

Historical role of MSF in Guinea

The MSF Head of Mission indicated that his organisation played a crucial role in humanitarian assistance to refugees fleeing the civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone, between 1990 and 2000, by building and managing camps in Nzérékoré, Guéckédou, Forécariah and Macenta. The organisation also put in place durable solutions for drinking water and sanitation in these camps.

Fight against HIV/AIDS in Conakry

At Donka, MSF created a centre of excellence for the treatment of advanced HIV. In 2023, 917 patients were hospitalised there, with a clear reduction in the mortality rate. Mr Matter also evoked the introduction of new diagnostic techniques and the continuous training of local doctors and nurses. He underlined the operational research efforts, notably on viral resistance, and insisted on the importance of free care and testing. MSF continues to train expert patients and to develop targeted strategies to reach vulnerable populations.

Response to epidemiological emergencies

Mr Matter specified that MSF works closely with the Ministry of Health and the National Health Security Agency (ANSS) to strengthen local capacities for epidemic management. He underlined the importance of continuous training of health professionals and the integration of operational research, in particular with the deployment of new services such as palliative care.

Malaria Project and capacity building in Kouroussa

As part of the fight against malaria in Kouroussa, MSF has concentrated its efforts on care, training of nursing staff, logistical and material support, as well as on strategies adapted to peaks of transmission. Julien Matter described this project as an illustration of MSF's commitment to long-term public health interventions.

Environmental health in Guinea

In Guinea, Médecins Sans Frontières also pays particular attention to environmental health. That is why it has built and rehabilitated boreholes, but has also become involved in the modern management of medical waste and in initiatives to raise awareness of good hygiene practices.

Independence and funding of MSF

With more than 50 years of experience, MSF works today in 70 countries, financed 98 per cent by private funds, thus guaranteeing its independence. Julien Matter recalled that MSF's interventions, based on "impartiality, neutrality and independence", put the patient at the centre of concerns and benefit from effective logistics allowing rapid intervention in the event of disaster or epidemic.

Through its diversified actions in Guinea, Médecins Sans Frontières continues to demonstrate its commitment to responding to urgent health needs while strengthening local capacities. The organisation works not only to provide immediate and essential care, but also over the long term, by promoting the training of health professionals and the development of sustainable infrastructure. By remaining faithful to its principles of independence, impartiality and neutrality, MSF strengthens its key role in the humanitarian response in Guinea, with the well-being of vulnerable populations and the resilience of local health systems in the face of public health challenges as its priority.

a1510.t:
Les résultats des élections américaines affecteront l’Ukraine plus que tout autre pays. Les candidats américains ont des points de vue différents sur le règlement du conflit russo-ukrainien. Kiev survivra-t-elle sous Donald Trump et que se passera-t-il si Kamala Harris gagne?
Un plan aux résultats imprévisibles. «Volodymyr Zelensky est le meilleur vendeur que le monde ait jamais connu, car chaque fois que Volodymyr Zelensky se rend aux États-Unis, il repart avec environ 60 milliards de dollars», a déclaré Donald Trump lors d’un rassemblement républicain en Pennsylvanie, rajoutant: «Il soutient le Parti démocrate et souhaite voir la vice-présidente Kamala Harris devenir la prochaine présidente des États-Unis».
La campagne électorale du candidat républicain reposait sur des critiques à l’égard du travail de l’administration de Joe Biden. En conséquence, si les démocrates allouaient une aide à Kiev, Donald Trump faisait le contraire et proposait une solution au conflit militaire qui n’affecterait pas le portefeuille des électeurs américains. L'ex-président et candidat est convaincu que la paix entre les pays viendra grâce à ses bonnes relations avec les dirigeants russe et ukrainien. «Si je gagne cette élection, la première chose que je ferai, c'est d'appeler Zelensky et le président Poutine et je leur dirai qu'ils doivent conclure un accord», a-t-il lancé. Il n'a pas précisé quels pourraient être les termes de cet accord. Cependant, la Russie exige que les «nouvelles réalités territoriales» soient reconnues, que les livraisons d’armes à Kiev cessent et que le statut de neutralité du pays soit consolidé.
Les exigences de l'Ukraine sont complètement opposées: garanties d'adhésion à l'OTAN, approvisionnement régulier en armes et accès aux frontières du début de 1991. Il sera extrêmement difficile de parvenir à un accord sur la seule «force de persuasion» du candidat républicain. Ici se pose la question suivante: jusqu’où ira-t-il pour tenir sa promesse électorale et entrer dans l’histoire comme l’homme qui a mis fin à la guerre au centre de l’Europe?
Comme Volodymyr Zelensky l’a admis, si Donald Trump arrive au pouvoir aux États-Unis, il existe un risque de réduction des livraisons d’armes à Kiev. Politico soulignait: «Trump envoie un signal fort, mais il ne soutiendra pas l’Ukraine et Zelensky contre Poutine». Et, sans le soutien américain, le conflit ne durera pas longtemps. Le pays ne disposera pas de suffisamment d’armes et de moyens de défense, ce qui entraînera une reddition progressive des positions. C’était déjà le cas l’année dernière lorsque les républicains du Congrès ont bloqué l’adoption d’un nouveau programme d’aide militaire.
Cependant, les paroles et les actions de Donald Trump sont souvent contradictoires. L’expression de Blaise Pascal, «Il ne faut pas le bruit d'un canon pour empêcher ses pensées. Il ne faut que le bruit d'une girouette ou d'une poulie», lui convient extrêmement bien. Dans les derniers jours avant les élections US, l'homme politique a soudainement commencé à dire qu'il n'était pas du tout amical avec la Russie. Il a récemment stipulé qu’il a «tué», «stoppé», le gazoduc Nord Stream. Par conséquent, pour entamer les négociations, Donald Trump peut faire pression - non pas sur Kiev - mais sur les partenaires commerciaux de la Russie qui seront contraints de se conformer aux sanctions américaines.
La candidate du Parti démocrate, Kamala Harris, a adopté une position fortement pro-ukrainienne. Elle refuse de mener des négociations directes avec le Kremlin. Lors d'une rencontre avec Volodymyr Zelensky, elle a souligné que le soutien à Kiev était un intérêt stratégique des États-Unis et non une œuvre de charité. «Nous soutenons l’Ukraine non pas par charité, mais parce que le peuple ukrainien et son avenir sont dans notre intérêt stratégique. Il est dans notre intérêt de respecter les règles et normes internationales», a déclaré Harris.
Selon elle, si Donald Trump était président, alors «Poutine serait actuellement à Kiev». «Soyons clairs. Il dit qu'il peut y mettre fin dès le premier jour. Savez-vous ce que cela signifie? Nous parlons de capitulation», a martelé la candidate démocrate. D’après ses déclarations, il ressort clairement que Washington continuera à aider l’Ukraine. Mais, ici se pose la question de savoir dans quelle mesure.
Au cours des trois dernières années, Kiev a eu le sentiment que l’aide américaine était calculée de manière à ce que l’Ukraine ne perde pas, tout en ne lui donnant pas la possibilité de gagner. On ne sait pas encore si la démocrate acceptera de «casser» ce système et de créer un déséquilibre dans les rapports de force.
D’un côté, Kamala Harris a tenu à faire savoir qu’elle ne poursuivrait pas le parcours politique de Joe Biden: «Comme tout nouveau président qui entre en fonction, j'apporterai mes expériences de vie, mes expériences professionnelles et des idées fraîches et nouvelles».
Et, elle ne pouvait pas promettre l’adhésion de Kiev à l’OTAN, notant seulement qu’elle aborderait cette question «quand et si le moment était venu».
Pour l’instant, une seule victoire des démocrates ne garantit pas à l’Ukraine le succès sur le front. La position du pays sera également affectée par les résultats des élections pour le vice-président. Si ce poste est occupé par J.D. Vance, un fervent partisan de Donald Trump, l’aide destinée à l’Ukraine risque à nouveau d’être «bloquée» au Congrès. L’avenir de l’État dépend, donc, des deux campagnes électorales.
En Ukraine, il existe un niveau élevé d'incertitude avec les élections américaines. Cela pèse sur l’avenir du pays. Le programme préliminaire des républicains est clair: Donald Trump et J.D. Vance ont déclaré vouloir mettre fin rapidement à la guerre russo-ukrainienne, ce qui implique de geler la situation le long de la ligne du front.
La situation d’Israël est devenue la priorité principale. Les nouveaux défis au Moyen-Orient occupent la politique US avant celle de l’Ukraine. BFMTV, faisant savoir la position de Kamala Harris où «elle paraît vouloir s'inscrire dans la continuité de Joe Biden», avertit que de grandes questions se posent à Kiev sur ce que cela pourrait signifier car la stratégie de Joe Biden peut difficilement être qualifiée d’efficace.
Récemment, Volodymyr Zelensky a indiqué que le pays n'avait reçu que 10% des 60 milliards de dollars approuvés en avril. Si Kamala Harris continue sur cette voie, le soutien des partenaires américains diminuera progressivement.
Au printemps, la situation atteindra un point où l'Ukraine sera obligée de redéfinir sa stratégie. Si Donald Trump gagne, le pays pourrait alors être poussé à conclure des accords rapides. Si les négociations voulues par Donald Trump échouent, celui-ci pourrait alors, hypothétiquement, passer à l’étape suivante.
Le candidat républicain à sa réélection, a fourni des Javelins à Kiev pendant son dernier mandat, ce que l’administration de Barack Obama n’a pas osé faire. Parmi les partisans du Parti républicain figurent les trois plus grandes entreprises militaires: Lockheed Martin, leader mondial de la production militaire, Northrop Grumman, développeur de technologies aérospatiales et Raytheon, fabricant du système de défense aérienne Patriot.
Les sponsors de Kamala Harris sont principalement des entreprises des secteurs du numérique et de l'informatique, et non du complexe militaro-industriel. Aussi, les responsables à Kiev sont dans l’attente des résultats US. Il est évident que l’ordre du jour changera, quel que soit le choix du président. Et le président ukrainien devra prendre des décisions basées sur la nouvelle réalité dans laquelle se trouvera l’État.
Philippe Rosenthal

a1510.en:
The results of the American elections will affect Ukraine more than any other country. The American candidates have different views on settling the Russo-Ukrainian conflict. Will Kyiv survive under Donald Trump, and what will happen if Kamala Harris wins?

A plan with unpredictable results. "Volodymyr Zelensky is the greatest salesman the world has ever known, because every time Volodymyr Zelensky goes to the United States, he leaves with about 60 billion dollars," Donald Trump declared at a Republican rally in Pennsylvania, adding: "He supports the Democratic Party and wants to see Vice President Kamala Harris become the next president of the United States."

The Republican candidate's election campaign was built on criticism of the work of Joe Biden's administration. Consequently, while the Democrats allocated aid to Kyiv, Donald Trump did the opposite and proposed a solution to the military conflict that would not affect American voters' wallets. The former president and candidate is convinced that peace between the countries will come thanks to his good relations with the Russian and Ukrainian leaders. "If I win this election, the first thing I will do is call Zelensky and President Putin and tell them they have to make a deal," he declared. He did not specify what the terms of that deal might be. However, Russia demands that the "new territorial realities" be recognised, that arms deliveries to Kyiv cease, and that the country's neutral status be consolidated.

Ukraine's demands are completely the opposite: guarantees of NATO membership, a regular supply of weapons, and access to the borders of early 1991. It will be extremely difficult to reach an agreement on the Republican candidate's "powers of persuasion" alone. This raises the following question: how far will he go to keep his campaign promise and enter history as the man who ended the war in the centre of Europe?

As Volodymyr Zelensky has admitted, if Donald Trump comes to power in the United States, there is a risk that arms deliveries to Kyiv will be reduced. Politico stressed: "Trump is sending a strong signal, but he will not support Ukraine and Zelensky against Putin." And without American support, the conflict will not last long. The country will not have enough weapons and means of defence, which will lead to a gradual surrender of positions. That was already the case last year when Republicans in Congress blocked the adoption of a new military aid programme.

However, Donald Trump's words and actions are often contradictory. Blaise Pascal's expression, "It does not take the noise of a cannon to stop his thoughts. It only takes the noise of a weathervane or a pulley," suits him extremely well. In the final days before the US elections, the politician suddenly began saying that he was not friendly with Russia at all. He recently stated that he had "killed" and "stopped" the Nord Stream pipeline. Therefore, in order to begin negotiations, Donald Trump may apply pressure - not on Kyiv - but on Russia's trading partners, who will be forced to comply with American sanctions.

The Democratic Party's candidate, Kamala Harris, has adopted a strongly pro-Ukrainian position. She refuses to hold direct negotiations with the Kremlin. During a meeting with Volodymyr Zelensky, she stressed that support for Kyiv was a strategic interest of the United States and not an act of charity. "We support Ukraine not out of charity, but because the Ukrainian people and their future are in our strategic interest. It is in our interest to uphold international rules and norms," Harris declared.

According to her, if Donald Trump were president, then "Putin would be in Kyiv right now." "Let's be clear. He says he can end it on day one. Do you know what that means? We are talking about capitulation," the Democratic candidate hammered home. From her statements it is clear that Washington will continue to help Ukraine. But here the question arises of to what extent.

Over the past three years, Kyiv has had the feeling that American aid was calculated in such a way that Ukraine would not lose, while not giving it the possibility of winning. It is not yet known whether the Democrat will agree to "break" this system and create an imbalance in the balance of forces.

On the one hand, Kamala Harris was keen to make it known that she would not continue Joe Biden's political course: "Like any new president who takes office, I will bring my life experiences, my professional experiences and fresh, new ideas."

And she could not promise Kyiv's accession to NATO, noting only that she would address that question "when and if the time comes."

For now, a Democratic victory alone does not guarantee Ukraine success at the front. The country's position will also be affected by the results of the vice-presidential election. If that post is held by J.D. Vance, a fervent supporter of Donald Trump, aid destined for Ukraine risks once again being "blocked" in Congress. The state's future therefore depends on both election campaigns.

In Ukraine there is a high level of uncertainty about the American elections. This weighs on the country's future. The Republicans' preliminary programme is clear: Donald Trump and J.D. Vance have said they want to end the Russo-Ukrainian war quickly, which implies freezing the situation along the front line.

Israel's situation has become the main priority. The new challenges in the Middle East occupy US policy ahead of Ukraine. BFMTV, reporting Kamala Harris's position, where "she appears to want to align herself with the continuity of Joe Biden," warns that big questions arise in Kyiv about what this could mean, because Joe Biden's strategy can hardly be described as effective.

Recently, Volodymyr Zelensky indicated that the country had received only 10% of the 60 billion dollars approved in April. If Kamala Harris continues along this path, support from American partners will gradually diminish.

By spring, the situation will reach a point where Ukraine will be obliged to redefine its strategy. If Donald Trump wins, the country could then be pushed into concluding quick deals. If the negotiations Donald Trump wants fail, he could then, hypothetically, move on to the next stage.

The Republican candidate for re-election supplied Javelins to Kyiv during his last term, something Barack Obama's administration did not dare to do. Among the Republican Party's supporters are the three largest military companies: Lockheed Martin, the world leader in military production; Northrop Grumman, a developer of aerospace technologies; and Raytheon, manufacturer of the Patriot air defence system.

Kamala Harris's sponsors are mainly companies from the digital and IT sectors, not from the military-industrial complex. So officials in Kyiv are waiting for the US results. It is obvious that the agenda will change, whichever president is chosen. And the Ukrainian president will have to take decisions based on the new reality in which the state finds itself.

Philippe Rosenthal

a1599.t:
Jennifer Rigby
Ange Kasongo
Sonia Rolley
LONDON/KINSHASA (Reuters)—Adults started getting vaccinations against mpox in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s capital this week. But there were no shots available for children, the most vulnerable group after a key dose donation was held back by an old legal hurdle.
Japan pledged in September to donate three million doses from its national stockpile of LC16m8 vaccines, first developed by local firm KM Biologics for smallpox.
It is the only vaccine effective against mpox approved for use in children, and the pledge was the biggest single donation yet to fight the disease anywhere.
However, the two countries took time to negotiate over a common issue in global health: who pays if the vaccine causes unexpected side-effects?
Congo said the issue has now been resolved. But the delay again showed the need for a better system, global health experts said, to stop seemingly technical points holding up life-saving responses.
Without clear terms, governments of poorer countries fear being left on the hook for claims. Donor governments are also often unwilling. But the payouts can be so huge, in the rare cases of problems, that an agreement over who is responsible needs to be signed before doses can be shipped.
Similar worries held up vaccine programmes during Covid-19.
“When I read the (donation) contract, I added that both countries must be responsible if any side-effects occur,” Congo’s health minister Samuel Roger Kamba Mulamba said in a press conference in Kinshasa earlier this month.
“That’s why it took so long, because it went back to Japan.” Now, “all the formalities have been completed,” he added.
‘Emergency Use’ Clearance
Japan’s government told Reuters earlier this month there was no current dispute about liability, without going into further detail, and that discussions over deliveries were ongoing. KM Biologics, the Japanese company which produced the vaccine, declined to comment.
Global health experts and industry representatives said there should be a better system set up in advance of major outbreaks to cover the liability issue.
“During a pandemic, well-designed, no-fault compensation systems are essential,” said Paula Barbosa, associate director of vaccine policy at the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA), an industry trade body.
Negotiating liability is a particular challenge during a crisis, when there is pressure to give new products quicker “emergency use” authorisations.
LC16m8 got emergency clearance from the World Health Organisation on Tuesday last week, and from Congo’s government in June. But vaccine manufacturers’ insurers will not cover side-effects’ claims for medicines which receive such expedited approvals.
The other vaccine being used for adults, developed by Bavarian Nordic, has received fuller approvals, so liability has not been an issue. Around three million doses of this shot have been pledged to Congo by governments including the U.S., and around 375,000 doses have arrived in the country – still far short of what African health officials say is needed.
But vaccinations with this shot have started slowly, with some at-risk communities in the vast country seemingly unaware of the push.
This may also be an issue for the Japanese donation for children, health officials in Congo and internationally said, although the need is urgent: children have made up the majority of the more than 1,100 suspected mpox deaths in Africa this year.
“It’s important for these vaccines to arrive quickly,” one doctor working on the response in Congo said. But, the doctor added, before widespread use, there should be tests on how to administer the vaccine, and a plan for where it would be most effective.
LC16m8 is given using a bifurcated needle, a technique that involves pricking the skin 15 times to deliver the vaccine, which will require some training of health workers. The needles are also being donated by Japan.
The Japanese government said on Tuesday it was “tackling and coordinating to solve these problems”, without giving further detail.
“We cannot tell you how to solve them immediately,” added Tatsuki Sato from the Ministry of Health.

a1601.t:
Malawi is grappling with the challenges of hosting around 4,000 Mozambican asylum seekers who have fled political unrest in Mozambique. This situation was highlighted during a visit to Nyamithuthu Refugee Camp in Nsanje by a high-level delegation, which included representatives from the British High Commission to Malawi, the UNHCR, USAID, and Malawi’s Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA).
The asylum seekers had initially been sheltered in schools, but this arrangement disrupted education, leading to their relocation to the Nyamithuthu camp in the traditional authority of Tengani. The camp now hosts those fleeing the violent aftermath of Mozambique’s contested October presidential elections, which triggered deadly protests.
The unrest has added to the political volatility in Mozambique, where opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane recently returned to Maputo from exile, following months of hiding due to the tensions. Mondlane’s return marks a pivotal moment in the ongoing political crisis, as Daniel Chapo of the ruling Frelimo party, confirmed as the election winner by the constitutional court, prepares to be sworn in as president.
At the Nyamithuthu camp, Mozambican asylum seekers, including Augushito Davite, 69, from Mchacha, and Patricia Lemeti, 42, from Kuntoso village in Morrumbala district, have expressed growing concern over their living conditions. The two, speaking on behalf of other asylum seekers, said the lack of food assistance is their most urgent need. “We are starving, the support being rendered is mostly non-food items,” they shared.
This food shortage has caught the attention of Malawi’s Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA). Hilda Katema, a senior administrative and operations manager in the Department for Refugees, acknowledged the crisis and assured that the government is committed to addressing the food needs of the asylum seekers.
Commissioner Charles Kalemba of DoDMA confirmed that his department, in collaboration with the Department for Refugees, is working to ensure that the asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu camp receive essential supplies, including food. Kalemba emphasized the department’s role in managing large numbers of people in camps and providing necessary expertise.
Gloria Nyang’iye, Associate Reporting Officer for UNHCR, also highlighted the progress in improving the camp’s shelter and sanitation facilities, ensuring a more stable environment for the asylum seekers. As the political crisis in Mozambique continues to unfold, the pressure on Malawi to provide for the increasing number of asylum seekers is mounting.
While significant efforts are being made to address immediate needs, such as food and shelter, the situation calls for sustained international support to ensure the wellbeing of those displaced by the violence in Mozambique. Malawi’s response to this refugee crisis will be crucial in determining its ability to manage both the humanitarian needs of the asylum seekers and its own economic and social stability.

a1742.t:
Le Hub Logistique du PAM à PK20 a abrité dimanche 2 février 2020, une cérémonie officielle de lancement de la formation en alternance d’un groupe de jeunes apprenantes de la filière CAP Magasinage-Entreposage du nouveau centre sectoriel de formation professionnelle dédié aux métiers du transport et de la logistique de la commune de Balbala.
Plusieurs hautes personnalités du MENFOP, du PAM et de l’Ambassade des Etats-Unis ont inauguré cette cérémonie de lancement. Il s’agissait notamment de MM. Mohamed Abdallah Mahyoub, Secrétaire Général du MENFOP ; Larry E. André , l’Ambassadeur des Etats-Unis à Djibouti ; Mutinta Chimuka, Représentante et Directrice du PAM à Djibouti ; M. Bert Ubamadu , Représentant et Directeur de l’USAID à Djibouti ; M. Jacques Collignon, le Responsable de la chaine d’approvisionnement du PAM à Djibouti. le Directeur Général de l’Enseignement Technique et de la Formation Professionnelle, Abdoulkader Houmed Abdoulkader , l’Inspecteur Général de l’Enseignement Technique et de la Formation Professionnelle Mahdi Omar Farah ainsi que divers autres responsables du MENFOP et du PAM ont également participé à la cérémonie.
Après un mot de bienvenue de M. Miguel Thomas , point focal du PAM pour le projet, la première partie de la cérémonie a été ponctuée par les interventions de Madame Mutinta Chimuka , la Représentante et Directrice du PAM à Djibouti ; de M. Larry E. Andre , l’Ambassadeur des Etats-Unis à Djibouti et de M. Mohamed Abdallah , le Secrétaire Général du MENFOP
Tous ont rappelé que cette formation en alternance s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet de formation professionnelle et de renforcement des capacités dans le secteur du transport et de la logistique mis en œuvre conjointement par le Ministère de l’Education Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle (MENFOP) et le Programme Alimentaire Mondial (PAM), avec l’appui financier de l’Agence des Etats Unis d’Amérique pour le Développement International (USAID) à Djibouti.
Plus généralement, elle répond à la stratégie de développement économique et social initiée par le Président de la République de Djibouti, Son Excellence Monsieur ISMAIL OMAR GUELLEH, et de sa détermination à faire de la formation professionnelle un levier de développement économique et un instrument de lutte contre le chômage et l’exclusion sociale des jeunes. La seconde partie a été marquée par la signature d’un Mémorandum d’Entente entre le MENFOP et le PAM. Ledit document a été paraphé par le Secrétaire Général du MENFOP et la représentante du PAM en présence de Son Excellence l’Ambassadeur des Etats-Unis d’Amérique à Djibouti.
Le Mémorandum d’Entente vise à formaliser un cadre de coopération entre le PAM et le MENFOP basé sur une volonté commune de renforcer les capacités du personnel formateurs de ce dernier en vue de la mise en place des formations professionnelles pour le secteur du transport et de la logistique à Djibouti.
Le PAM en collaboration avec le Ministère de l’éducation nationale et de la formation professionnelle contribue au développement d’une main-d’œuvre locale, qualifiée et rapidement employable dans les différentes spécialités de formation relevant du secteur des transports et de la logistique pour répondre aux besoins des entreprises logistiques basées à Djibouti, tout en atteignant l’objectif “zéro faim”.
Ce nouveau centre est opérationnel depuis janvier 2020 et accueille 302 apprenants dans les différentes spécialités de formation en transport et logistique. Cet établissement vient donc renforcer le dispositif de formation du Ministère de l’Education Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle.
A travers ce Mémorandum d’Entente, les deux parties s’engagent à renforcer leur coopération en vue de :
coordonner et mettre en place des programmes de formation pratique du transport et de la logistique au Hub Logistique du PAM à PK20 afin de développer le professionnalisme des apprenantes, initier et sensibiliser les apprenantes du MENFOP qui participent aux formations au monde professionnelle à travers la participation de celles-ci aux activités logistiques et de transport du PAM au Hub Logistique de PK20. Le PAM et le MENFOP s’accorderont sur une inclusion des élèves du MENFOP au Programme d’innovation technologique dans le domaine logistique comme le fonctionnement des silos ou la conservation innovantes des denrées alimentaires par de nouvelles techniques de bâches.
Enfin, la dernière partie de la cérémonie a été l’occasion pour les personnalités présentes de voir les jeunes apprenantes en action. Tous ont été éblouis par les capacités démontrées par les jeunes sur le terrain et ont été par ailleurs agréablement surpris de constater que le groupe de jeunes bénéficiaires était exclusivement composé de jeunes filles.
Un moment solennel pour apprécier et se féliciter des résultats de la politique du Ministère de l’Education Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle (MENFOP) en matière de promotion du genre, et plus particulièrement de l’intégration des filles dans les filières de formation professionnelle préparant à des métiers jusqu’à alors uniquement réservés aux hommes.
MAS
a1742.en:
The WFP Logistics Hub at PK20 hosted, on Sunday 2 February 2020, an official ceremony launching the work-study training of a group of young female learners in the CAP Warehousing-Storage stream of the new sectoral vocational training centre dedicated to transport and logistics occupations in the commune of Balbala.

Several senior figures from MENFOP, WFP and the United States Embassy inaugurated this launch ceremony. They included Mr Mohamed Abdallah Mahyoub, Secretary General of MENFOP; Larry E. Andre, United States Ambassador to Djibouti; Mutinta Chimuka, WFP Representative and Country Director in Djibouti; Mr Bert Ubamadu, USAID Representative and Director in Djibouti; and Mr Jacques Collignon, WFP Supply Chain Manager in Djibouti. The Director General of Technical Education and Vocational Training, Abdoulkader Houmed Abdoulkader, the Inspector General of Technical Education and Vocational Training, Mahdi Omar Farah, as well as various other MENFOP and WFP officials, also took part in the ceremony.

After a welcome address by Mr Miguel Thomas, WFP focal point for the project, the first part of the ceremony was punctuated by remarks from Ms Mutinta Chimuka, WFP Representative and Country Director in Djibouti; Mr Larry E. Andre, United States Ambassador to Djibouti; and Mr Mohamed Abdallah, Secretary General of MENFOP.

All recalled that this work-study training forms part of the vocational training and capacity-building project in the transport and logistics sector implemented jointly by the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP) and the World Food Programme (WFP), with the financial support of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Djibouti.

More broadly, it responds to the economic and social development strategy initiated by the President of the Republic of Djibouti, His Excellency Mr ISMAIL OMAR GUELLEH, and to his determination to make vocational training a lever for economic development and an instrument in the fight against unemployment and the social exclusion of young people. The second part was marked by the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between MENFOP and WFP. The document was initialled by the Secretary General of MENFOP and the WFP representative in the presence of His Excellency the Ambassador of the United States of America to Djibouti.

The Memorandum of Understanding aims to formalise a framework of cooperation between WFP and MENFOP based on a shared desire to strengthen the capacities of the latter's training staff with a view to setting up vocational training for the transport and logistics sector in Djibouti.

WFP, in collaboration with the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training, is contributing to the development of a local, qualified and readily employable workforce in the various training specialities of the transport and logistics sector, in order to meet the needs of logistics companies based in Djibouti, while achieving the "zero hunger" objective.

This new centre has been operational since January 2020 and hosts 302 learners in the various transport and logistics training specialities. The establishment therefore strengthens the training system of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training.

Through this Memorandum of Understanding, the two parties undertake to strengthen their cooperation with a view to: coordinating and setting up practical transport and logistics training programmes at the WFP Logistics Hub at PK20 in order to develop the professionalism of the learners; and introducing and familiarising the MENFOP learners who take part in the training with the professional world through their participation in WFP logistics and transport activities at the PK20 Logistics Hub. WFP and MENFOP will agree on the inclusion of MENFOP students in the technological innovation programme in the logistics field, such as the operation of silos or innovative food preservation through new tarpaulin techniques.

Finally, the last part of the ceremony was an opportunity for the dignitaries present to see the young learners in action. All were dazzled by the abilities demonstrated by the young people in the field and were also pleasantly surprised to note that the group of young beneficiaries was made up exclusively of young women.

A solemn moment to appreciate and welcome the results of the policy of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP) on gender promotion, and more particularly the integration of girls into vocational training streams preparing them for occupations until now reserved solely for men.

MAS

a1773.t:
From Maritime Silk Road Hub to “Trade Window”: Guangdong’s Continuous Push for Opening Up
Since the Tang Dynasty (618-907), Guangzhou in Guangdong Province has been a prominent port where Sino-foreign trade flourished, attracting numerous foreign merchants who traveled here along the Maritime Silk Road.
Following the founding of the People’s Republic of China, Guangdong continued to serve as China’s “trade window.” To earn foreign exchange and meet the country’s urgent demand for various imported materials necessary for large-scale economic construction, Guangdong capitalized on its geographical proximity to Hong Kong and Macao to host three export fairs from October 1955 to May 1956. In this context, officials from the former Ministry of Foreign Trade and the Guangdong Provincial Government considered hosting a national export fair in Guangzhou.
From April 25 to May 25, 1957, the first Canton Fair took place, covering an exhibition area of 9,600 square meters and showcasing 10,900 categories of goods. The event attracted 1,223 buyers from 19 countries and regions, achieving an export turnover of $17.54 million. Today, the Canton Fair stands as the longest-running and largest comprehensive international trade exhibition in China, often regarded as “China’s No. 1 Exhibition.” As of the first half of 2024, this grand event has successfully hosted 135 sessions, established trade relations with 229 countries and regions worldwide, achieved a cumulative export turnover of approximately $1.5 trillion, and attracted over 9.3 million overseas participants. The fair has significantly enhanced trade exchanges and fostered friendly ties between China and other countries and regions across the globe.
In 2015, the China (Guangdong) Pilot Free Trade Zone was established in Shenzhen, Guangdong, making it one of the second batch of pilot free trade zones approved in China. Johannes Jozef Bults, a Dutch entrepreneur engaged in import and export in the Qianhai and Shekou Area of Shenzhen, an integral part of the pilot free trade zone, noted that since the establishment of the zone, he has witnessed a continuous optimization of the business environment. “The government’s support, from company registration to everyday operations, has made it incredibly convenient for entrepreneurs to do business here,” he remarked.
Gu Qingyang, an associate professor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy at the National University of Singapore, expressed that China is currently at a critical stage of development. He anticipates that Guangdong will continue to embody the pioneering spirit of innovation and exploration, boldly venturing into avenues for high-quality development in China.
Since 2024, the term “new quality productive forces” has become a frequently discussed theme in economic plans across various sectors and regions in Guangdong. The province is dedicated to developing the manufacturing industry and prioritizing the real economy, aiming to build a modern industrial system with international competitiveness and accelerate the formation of “new quality productive forces.” Additionally, Guangdong is committed to enhancing the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, focusing on strengthening major infrastructure connectivity, improving foreign trade cooperation, accelerating industrial investment, and promoting collaboration in marine sectors. The province is also working to continually improve its maritime, land, and air transportation while leading in institutional openness regarding rules, regulations, management, and standards within the Greater Bay Area.
The spirit of openness from the Maritime Silk Road continues to thrive. Today, Guangdong has become a microcosm of China’s reform and opening-up, serving as a vital window for the world to understand and engage with China.
